origin.description: xy resamples rows, wxy weights rows by rexp, and jack deletes about 2*sqrt(n) rows. Each replicate is the same linear program.
origin.details: xy resamples rows, wxy weights rows by rexp, and jack deletes about 2*sqrt(n) rows. Each replicate is the same linear program.
origin.value: boot.rq R=3 xy, R=2 wxy, and R=2 jack on the n=40 design, set.seed(1)
origin.example:
set.seed(1)
xy <- as.numeric(boot.rq(X, y, tau=0.5, R=3)$B)
set.seed(1)
wxy <- as.numeric(boot.rq(X, y, tau=0.5, R=2, bsmethod="wxy")$B)
set.seed(1)
jack <- as.numeric(boot.rq(X, y, tau=0.5, R=2, bsmethod="jack")$B)
c(xy, wxy, jack)

translation.example:
from quantreg import boot_rq
set_seed(1)
xy = boot_rq(X, y, tau=0.5, r=3)["B"].ravel(order="F")
set_seed(1)
wxy = boot_rq(X, y, tau=0.5, r=2, bsmethod="wxy")["B"].ravel(order="F")
set_seed(1)
jack = boot_rq(X, y, tau=0.5, r=2, bsmethod="jack")["B"].ravel(order="F")
return np.concatenate([xy, wxy, jack])
